reason: The commit expands GIF frame copying from four explicitly supported pixel depths (8, 16, 24, and 32 bits per pixel) to every byte-aligned format up to 512 bits per pixel. The existing harness always uses `ic.pixcfg` returned by `decode_image_config` and never varies the destination pixel format, so it does not adequately exercise the newly accepted pixel-format space.
evidence: The old implementation accepted only `bits_per_pixel` values 8, 16, 24, and 32.
The new condition accepts any `bits_per_pixel <= 512` for which `(bits_per_pixel & 7) == 0`, then derives `bytes_per_pixel` using `bits_per_pixel >> 3`.
`gif_fuzzer.c` allocates and initializes the pixel buffer directly from `ic.pixcfg` and passes it to `wuffs_gif__decoder__decode_frame`; it has no fuzz-controlled pixel-format selection.
recommended_action: Extend the GIF harness to exercise `decode_frame` with fuzz-selected valid byte-aligned destination pixel formats, including newly supported depths, while sizing and initializing `pixcfg` and the pixel buffer consistently and retaining allocation limits.
